Dispel Magic can remove Paige’s eligible root or a pending removable item disable. Clear the effect to restore movement, then leave the dangerous angle. Dispel Magic can remove eligible trap or root pressure that makes Grey Talon’s next shot easy to land. Clear it and restore your route to cover. The cleanse does not block the next arrow or owl if you remain exposed; those need positioning, spirit protection or a timed ultimate response.

Dispel Magic clears Binding Word’s removable setup before it secures lethal follow-up. Move out of the winning angle afterward. Dispel Magic clears Stalker’s Mark and eligible overlapping non-ultimate debuffs; Divine Barrier has a separate role against the ultimate effect. Reposition toward help after cleansing. Dispel Magic clears meaningful eligible knife, dash and item debuffs from Shiv. Dispel Magic is the focused lane response when Static Charge repeatedly sets up a kill. Clear the pending stun while you can act, then reach cover so the follow-up angle is worse. Avoid staying beside the wave; the cleanse does not stop new area damage or a later application.

Dispel Magic is the response to Light Eater when that debuff enables Celeste’s follow-up damage. Clear the important setup, then change angle before she reapplies it. A cleanse does not ground her or make sustained gunfire harmless; those threats call for separate access or weapon-control answers.

Dispel Magic is useful for Wrecked when the debuff makes Billy’s follow-up lethal. Clear it and reset your position rather than accepting another close trade immediately. His ultimate needs its own movement or timed-protection plan; removing Wrecked does not automatically end the whole sequence.
